claim: Without BAR1-P2P patches, cuDeviceCanAccessPeer and cuCtxEnablePeerAccess return 0 / CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_UNSUPPORTED (217) on all six ordered pairs and nvidia-smi topo -p2p r reports GNS, yet an alias-proof cuMemcpyPeer passes on all six pairs because the driver stages the copy through host memory.
stance_target: the repo's 'no P2P' premise in the default unlocked configuration, and the mechanism by which collectives still work (host staging) despite peer access being unavailable
scope_conditions: 3x CMP 170HX memory-unlocked to 65,536 MiB, all Gen2 x16, GPU0/GPU1 behind one PLX PEX 8747 and GPU2 behind a second, ACS at firmware default with ReqRedir+/CmpltRedir+ enabled (ACSCtl 0x001d), driver 615.71.09 + upstream cmpunlocker 88e39ce + rebar-serialize.patch, no BAR1-P2P patches
quoted_support: | `canAccessPeer` / `enablePeerAccess` | 0 / `CUDA_ERROR_PEER_ACCESS_UNSUPPORTED` (217) on all 6 pairs; `nvidia-smi topo -p2p r` = GNS | | Alias-proof copy | pass on all 6 pairs (driver stages through host memory) |

claim: NCCL all-reduce bus bandwidth at 256 MiB measures 3.69 GB/s on a same-switch pair, 3.85 GB/s on a cross-switch pair and 4.24 GB/s across all three cards, with NCCL selecting SHM/direct transport for every pair.
stance_target: the all-reduce bandwidth DDP gradient reduction would actually get on this box — the load-bearing number for the repo's DDP-feasibility arithmetic
scope_conditions: 3x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x16, no BAR1-P2P, torch 2.13.0+cu130 / NCCL 2.29.7 under torchrun, bf16 sum, 5 warm-ups, median of 20, bus bandwidth = algbw x 2(n-1)/n
quoted_support: | NCCL all-reduce 256 MiB, busbw | 3.69 GB/s same-switch pair, 3.85 GB/s cross-switch pair, 4.24 GB/s all three | | NCCL transport | SHM/direct for every pair |

claim: Small-message all-reduce latency is 144 us (same-switch pair), 120 us (cross-switch pair) and 134 us (all three) at 8 KiB, and cuMemcpyPeer latency is 22 us / 40 us / 343 us at 4 KiB / 64 KiB / 1 MiB versus a D2H reference of 9.5 / 18.4 / 165 us.
stance_target: the latency floor for any per-step collective on this fabric — at 8 KiB, a 5-GPU DDP all-reduce would cost on the order of 100+ us per collective regardless of message size
scope_conditions: 3x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x16, no P2P; latency measured with cuMemcpyPeer synchronised on both contexts, median of 30 (<=16 MiB) or 8 copies
quoted_support: | `cuMemcpyPeer`, 4 KiB / 64 KiB / 1 MiB | 22 µs / 40 µs / 343 µs (D2H: 9.5 / 18.4 / 165 µs) | ... | NCCL all-reduce 8 KiB | 144 µs / 120 µs / 134 µs |

claim: Same-switch and cross-switch copy bandwidth differ by no more than 1% (6.21-6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB against a single-card D2H reference of 6.68 GB/s) because nothing takes the switch-local path when P2P is unavailable.
stance_target: whether PCIe switch topology can be exploited to reduce collective cost on this box — without P2P it cannot, so switch-aware placement buys nothing
scope_conditions: 3x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x16 behind two PLX PEX 8747 switches, no BAR1-P2P; nvidia-smi topo -m reports GPU0-GPU1 PIX and GPU0/1-GPU2 PHB
quoted_support: | `cuMemcpyPeer`, 256 MiB | 6.21–6.30 GB/s (single-card D2H: 6.68 GB/s) | ... | Same switch vs cross switch | no difference (≤1 %) — nothing takes the switch-local path |

claim: The authors state two limitations: true BAR1 P2P (community fork patches) was untested here, so this is the no-P2P baseline for that comparison, and there was one probe run per pair with no cross-run error bars.
stance_target: the confidence tier of the all-reduce numbers — they are single-run measurements on a no-P2P baseline, not a repeated comparison against the P2P-enabled path
scope_conditions: As stated in the receipt's Limitations section
quoted_support: - True BAR1 P2P (community fork patches) was **untested** here; this is the no-P2P baseline for that comparison. - One probe run per pair; no cross-run error bars.
